translations.text: ᚦ (Thorn) is very sharp. For every thane, taking hold of it is bad, and it is beyond measure cruel to any man who lies down among it.
ᛋ (Sun) is always a hope to seafarers when they carry it over the fish's bath, until the sea-steed brings them to land.
ᛞ (Day) is the Lord's messenger, dear to men, the glorious light of the Creator, a joy and a hope to rich and poor, of use to all.
ᚪ (Oak) on earth is food for the flesh of the children of men. It often travels over the gannet's bath, and the ocean tests whether the oak keeps noble faith.
ᚫ (Ash) is very tall and dear to men. It stands firm on its base and holds its place rightly, though many men fight against it.
ᚣ (Yr) is a joy and an honour to every prince and nobleman. It looks fine on a horse, is dependable on a journey, and is a piece of war-gear.
ᛡ (Ior) is a river-fish, and yet it always takes its food on land. It has a fair dwelling surrounded by water, where it lives in joy.
